IDE Interface

This document defines the motherboard parallel ATA interface in I/O slot 11. Return to the main page.

Revision 2.0 follows memory map 2.2 and adds MC68450 channel-0 DMA while retaining PIO mode 0. The ATA byte lanes are crossed so direct sector DMA has the same byte order as 68000 memory. A CD74ACT157E forces the ATA data-register address during DMA, the PALCE20V8 reverses the strobe and buffer direction under ACK0_n, and two added HCT packages supply READY, the DIOW trailing edge, and drive reset. ATA DMARQ, DMACK, multiword DMA, and UDMA remain unused.

1. Compatibility

The connector and control signals follow the parallel ATA host interface. The BIOS starts each device in its reset transfer mode and uses PIO mode 0 for both processor and DMA data cycles. ATA hard disks, solid-state disks, and ATAPI optical drives share the same electrical interface. A passive 44-pin adapter can connect a 2.5-inch drive, and a True IDE adapter can connect a CompactFlash card. A SATA device needs an active PATA-to-SATA bridge.

Both device positions work. Firmware selects device 0 or device 1 with the Device/Head register. Drives may use master/slave jumpers. Cable Select requires a cable that routes pin 28 for that purpose, such as a standard 80-conductor ATA cable. The host timing does not depend on cable detection, so 40-conductor and 80-conductor cables both work at PIO mode 0.

Device capacity, geometry, command set, removable-media status, and logical sector size come from IDENTIFY DEVICE or IDENTIFY PACKET DEVICE. The design fixes no drive model or capacity. Firmware must reject a device whose IDENTIFY data does not report a command path it implements.

2. Architecture

system D15..D8 <-> HCT245 <-> ATA DD7..DD0
system D7..D0  <-> HCT245 <-> ATA DD15..DD8
CPU A3..A1 or 000 --> ACT157 --> HCT244 --> ATA DA2..DA0
ACK0_n ---------------^ select: high = CPU A3..A1, low = 000
IO11_n, A4, IDE_A3..A1, UDS_n, LDS_n, IDE_RW, ACK0_n --> PALCE20V8
MFP_CLK_5 --> HCT164 --> PAL timing taps QB and QE
PAL --> IDE_CS0_n, IDE_CS1_n, IDE_DIOR_n, IDE_BUF_DIR, IDE_BUF_OE_n
PAL IDE_DTACK_n ------------------------------> CPU completion tree
PAL IDE_DIOW_RAW_n + ACK0_n + DTC_n --> HCT32, HCT04 --> ATA DIOW_n
IDE_QE + ATA IORDY --> HCT08, HCT04 --> IDE_READY_n --> ACT157 4A
motherboard DTACK_n -----------------------------------> ACT157 4B
ACT157 4Y + BGACK_n --> HCT32 --> PCL0_n at the MC68450
ATA INTRQ --> HCT04 inverter --> level-2 priority input

IO11_n supplies the protected slot select. The IDE adapter sees supervisor cycles because the top I/O decoder suppresses user cycles before it asserts IO11_n. The motherboard timeout ends a transfer with a bus error if a selected device holds IORDY low for 51.2 microseconds.

3. Register Map

CPU address lines A3..A1 drive ATA DA2..DA0 through U_IDE_BUS. A4 selects the command block or the control block. The command-block data register uses a 16-bit word. The remaining registers use D15..D8 at even addresses because the lane crossing moves ATA DD7..DD0 to the 68000 upper lane.

Canonical ATA register addresses
68k address ATA select DA2..DA0 Read Write Width
$F60000 CS0_n 000 Data Data 16-bit word
$F60002 CS0_n 001 Error Features Upper byte
$F60004 CS0_n 010 Sector Count Sector Count Upper byte
$F60006 CS0_n 011 LBA Low LBA Low Upper byte
$F60008 CS0_n 100 LBA Mid LBA Mid Upper byte
$F6000A CS0_n 101 LBA High LBA High Upper byte
$F6000C CS0_n 110 Device Device Upper byte
$F6000E CS0_n 111 Status Command Upper byte
$F6001C CS1_n 110 Alternate Status Device Control Upper byte
$F6001E CS1_n 111 Device Address Reserved Upper byte

The PAL decodes A4..A1 and ignores A16..A5, so the 32-byte register pattern repeats through the slot. Firmware uses the canonical addresses above. A byte access to the data register receives no IDE_DTACK_n and reaches the motherboard timeout. Word accesses to an 8-bit register transfer the upper byte and leave the lower byte undefined.

4. Data Path and Byte Order

U_IDE_DATA_LO connects ATA DD7..DD0 to system D15..D8. U_IDE_DATA_HI connects ATA DD15..DD8 to system D7..D0. Both parts are SN74HCT245N. Their A ports face ATA, their B ports face the processor, and IDE_BUF_DIR drives both DIR pins. Two cascaded gates in U_IDE_IRQ buffer processor R/W into IDE_RW, and the PAL combines IDE_RW with ACK0_n to make IDE_BUF_DIR. A PIO read and a DMA transfer into memory both drive A to B. A PIO write and a DMA transfer out of memory both drive B to A. IDE_BUF_OE_n enables both parts during a valid PIO or DMA cycle.

The crossed lanes place ATA sector byte zero at the lower memory address, so sector PIO and DMA use the same memory image and need no per-word sector swap. This wiring deliberately reverses the apparent bit positions of a 16-bit ATA word at the CPU. Firmware byte-swaps numeric IDENTIFY words when interpreting them and handles ATA strings, ATAPI packets, and ATAPI responses according to each format instead of applying one blanket rule.

Place 33 ohm series resistors between each transceiver A-side cable route and the ATA header. The transceivers isolate the processor bus from cable loading. The switched drive-power harness powers the selected drive before firmware accesses this interface.

5. PAL, Multiplexer, and Timing Control

U_IDE_CTRL is a PALCE20V8Q-15JC/4 in a 28-pin PLCC socket. The CUPL listing below is the source of record for the programmed equations and pin assignment. The PAL uses combinational mode with permanently enabled outputs. Revision 2.0 spends the last free input, physical pin 27, on ACK0_n. All eight macrocells are now allocated, so IDE_RESET_n, IDE_READY_n, and the DIOW trailing edge moved to discrete HCT gates.

PALCE20V8 PLCC assignment
Pins Signals Use
2, 3, 4, 5, 6 IO11_n, IDE_A1, IDE_A2, IDE_A3, A4 Slot and register decode
7, 9, 10 IDE_RW, UDS_n, LDS_n Direction and transfer width
11, 12, 13 IDE_QB, IDE_QE, IDE_IORDY Strobe and completion timing
16, 17 PERIPH_RESET_n, IDE_RESET_PULSE_n Cycle inhibit and stretched drive reset
27 ACK0_n MC68450 channel-0 acknowledge; the last free input, CUPL logical pin 23
18, 19, 20, 21 IDE_CYCLE, IDE_CS0_n, IDE_CS1_n, IDE_DIOR_n Cycle and read controls
23, 24, 25, 26 IDE_DIOW_RAW_n, IDE_DTACK_n, IDE_BUF_OE_n, IDE_BUF_DIR Ungated write strobe, completion, buffer enable, buffer direction
1, 8, 15, 22 No connection PLCC package no-connect pins
14, 28 Ground, +5 V Supply; 100 nF bypass at the socket

Physical PLCC pins map to CUPL 24-pin logical numbers by removing the four no-connect pins: physical 2 through 7 are logical 1 through 6, physical 9 through 14 are logical 7 through 12, physical 16 through 21 are logical 13 through 18, and physical 23 through 28 are logical 19 through 24. Keep the two numbering systems distinct in the schematic, the fitter report, and the build record.

Complete CUPL Source

Name     IDE_CONTROL;
PartNo   002;
Date     2026-09-12;
Revision 02;
Designer m68k-computer;
Company  None;
Assembly None;
Location U_IDE_CTRL;
Device   g20v8;

/* CUPL uses 24-pin logical numbers. The fitter maps them to PLCC pins. */

PIN 1  = IO11_n;
PIN 2  = IDE_A1;
PIN 3  = IDE_A2;
PIN 4  = IDE_A3;
PIN 5  = A4;
PIN 6  = IDE_RW;
PIN 7  = UDS_n;
PIN 8  = LDS_n;
PIN 9  = IDE_QB;
PIN 10 = IDE_QE;
PIN 11 = IDE_IORDY;
PIN 13 = PERIPH_RESET_n;
PIN 14 = IDE_RESET_PULSE_n;
PIN 23 = ACK0_n;

PIN 15 = IDE_CYCLE;
PIN 16 = IDE_CS0_n;
PIN 17 = IDE_CS1_n;
PIN 18 = IDE_DIOR_n;
PIN 19 = IDE_DIOW_RAW_n;
PIN 20 = IDE_DTACK_n;
PIN 21 = IDE_BUF_OE_n;
PIN 22 = IDE_BUF_DIR;

RUN        = PERIPH_RESET_n & IDE_RESET_PULSE_n;
DATA_REG   = !A4 & !IDE_A3 & !IDE_A2 & !IDE_A1;
BYTE_CYCLE = !UDS_n;
WORD_CYCLE = !UDS_n & !LDS_n;

PIO_CYCLE = !IO11_n & RUN
          & ((!DATA_REG & BYTE_CYCLE) # (DATA_REG & WORD_CYCLE));
DMA_CYCLE = !ACK0_n & RUN;
CYCLE     = PIO_CYCLE # DMA_CYCLE;

PIO_READ      = PIO_CYCLE & IDE_RW;
PIO_WRITE     = PIO_CYCLE & !IDE_RW;
DMA_DEV_READ  = DMA_CYCLE & !IDE_RW;
DMA_DEV_WRITE = DMA_CYCLE & IDE_RW;

IDE_CYCLE      = CYCLE;
IDE_CS0_n      = !((PIO_CYCLE & !A4) # DMA_CYCLE);
IDE_CS1_n      = !(PIO_CYCLE & A4);
IDE_DIOR_n     = !((PIO_READ # DMA_DEV_READ) & IDE_QB);
IDE_DIOW_RAW_n = !((PIO_WRITE # DMA_DEV_WRITE) & IDE_QB);
IDE_DTACK_n    = !(PIO_CYCLE & IDE_QE & IDE_IORDY);
IDE_BUF_OE_n   = !CYCLE;
IDE_BUF_DIR    = (ACK0_n & IDE_RW) # (!ACK0_n & !IDE_RW);

RUN, DATA_REG, PIO_CYCLE, DMA_CYCLE, and CYCLE are intermediate expressions. CUPL expands them into each output's sum of products instead of routing them through a pin, so no equation depends on output feedback. Simple mode gives every macrocell eight product terms and leaves pins 15 and 22 without feedback, which this listing does not need.

Product terms per output against the eight available
Output Terms Expansion
IDE_CYCLE, IDE_BUF_OE_n 6 Five from PIO_CYCLE and one from DMA_CYCLE
IDE_CS0_n 5 Four PIO terms that survive !A4, plus DMA
IDE_CS1_n 4 PIO terms that survive A4; DMA drops out
IDE_DIOR_n, IDE_DIOW_RAW_n 6 Five PIO terms and one DMA term, each gated by QB
IDE_DTACK_n 5 PIO terms gated by QE and IORDY; no DMA term
IDE_BUF_DIR 2 One term per ownership state

!DATA_REG expands to four terms, one each for A4, IDE_A3, IDE_A2, and IDE_A1, so PIO_CYCLE costs five product terms and DMA_CYCLE costs one. The PALCE20V8 has programmable output polarity, so an active-low output carries the same term count as the active-high function it inverts. The environment used to write this revision has no compatible CUPL fitter, so these counts are hand expansions. JEDEC fit, fuse checksum, and programmer verification remain build checks.

Address Multiplexer

During ACK0_n the shared address bus carries the DRAM address, so the ATA register address cannot come from A3..A1. U_IDE_DA_MUX, a CD74ACT157E, selects the source. ACT inputs accept the TTL levels that the processor and the MC68450 produce. Pin 1 is the common select and takes ACK0_n directly: a low select passes the A inputs, a high select passes the B inputs. Ground pin 15 so the outputs stay enabled.

U_IDE_DA_MUX channel assignment
A input, DMA B input, PIO and idle Output
2, ground 3, CPU A1 4, IDE_A1
5, ground 6, CPU A2 7, IDE_A2
11, ground 10, CPU A3 9, IDE_A3
14, IDE_READY_n 13, DTACK_n 12, IDE_PCL_MUX

The three address outputs drive U_IDE_BUS and the PAL decode inputs. A DMA cycle therefore presents ATA DA2..DA0 = 000, the data register, with CS0_n asserted by the DMA_CYCLE term and CS1_n held inactive. Driven selection replaces the cable-side pull-downs that a passive scheme would need. The fourth channel carries the READY source below, which needs the same select.

Discrete Glue

U_IDE_GATE is an SN74HCT08N and U_IDE_OR is an SN74HCT32N. Both sit beside the PAL. The three spare inverters in U_IDE_IRQ supply the inversions. 

IDE_RESET_n   = PERIPH_RESET_n AND IDE_RESET_PULSE_n
IDE_READY     = IDE_QE AND IDE_IORDY
IDE_READY_n   = NOT IDE_READY
IDE_DMA_END_n = ACK0_n OR DTC_n
IDE_DMA_END   = NOT IDE_DMA_END_n
IDE_DIOW_n    = IDE_DIOW_RAW_n OR IDE_DMA_END

IDE_PCL_MUX   = IDE_READY_n  while ACK0_n = 0
IDE_PCL_MUX   = DTACK_n      while ACK0_n = 1
PCL0_n        = IDE_PCL_MUX OR BGACK_n
Added gate allocation
Package and gate Pins Function
U_IDE_GATE gate 1 1, 2 to 3 IDE_RESET_n to U_IDE_BUS pin 17
U_IDE_GATE gate 2 4, 5 to 6 IDE_READY, active high
U_IDE_GATE gates 3 and 4 9, 10 to 8; 12, 13 to 11 Unused: inputs grounded, outputs open
U_IDE_OR gate 1 1, 2 to 3 IDE_DMA_END_n from ACK0 and DTC
U_IDE_OR gate 2 4, 5 to 6 IDE_DIOW_n to U_IDE_BUS pin 15
U_IDE_OR gate 3 9, 10 to 8 PCL0_n to MC68450 pin 5
U_IDE_OR gate 4 12, 13 to 11 Unused: inputs to +5 V, output open
U_IDE_IRQ gates 4, 5, 6 Three remaining inverters IDE_DMA_END, IDE_READY_n, and one spare with its input grounded

ACK0_n is an MC68450 output that stays driven, so it needs no board bias. DTC_n is three-stated while the processor owns the bus and carries the 10 kohm pull-up listed in DMA Controller, which holds IDE_DMA_END_n high through every PIO cycle. BGACK_n forces PCL0_n inactive whenever the processor owns the bus, so ordinary CPU completions do not toggle the MC68450 PCL input. The PCL transition bit still sets on the transitions that do occur; firmware ignores that bit on a channel programmed for READY and clears it with the rest of CSR.

Sequencer and PIO Timing

U_IDE_SEQ is a CD74HCT164E. Tie serial inputs A and B high, connect MFP_CLK_5 to CLK, and connect IDE_CYCLE to active-low CLR. QB at pin 4 becomes high on the second rising clock edge after the PAL accepts a cycle. QE at pin 10 becomes high on the fifth edge. Ending the cycle drives CLR low and clears both taps without waiting for a clock. Revision 2.0 moves the PAL completion input from QD to QE because only one tap input remains and the DMA READY term needs the longer delay. PIO cycles grow by two 5 MHz periods as a result.

The first sampling edge falls anywhere in the 200 ns period after the cycle starts, so QB arrives 200 ns to 400 ns after the start and QE arrives 800 ns to 1000 ns after it. At the oscillator's +100 ppm limit one period is 199.98 ns; the figures below use the four-period worst case of 799.92 ns for QE.

PIO mode 0 timing produced by the adapter
Interval Adapter value PIO mode 0 minimum
Chip select and address before read/write strobe At least one 5 MHz period, less logic skew 70 ns
DIOR_n or DIOW_n before completion Three 5 MHz periods, about 600 ns 290 ns
Transfer cycle At least five 5 MHz periods plus CPU release 600 ns

The PAL holds IDE_DTACK_n high while IDE_IORDY is low. A 4.7 kohm pull-up at the motherboard receiver supplies the ready state for a device that does not drive the line. U_IDE_BUS, an SN74HCT244N, buffers DA2..DA0, both chip selects, both strobes, and reset onto the cable. The three address outputs also feed PAL inputs IDE_A3..IDE_A1 before their series resistors. Tie both output-enable pins low.

U_IDE_BUS channel assignment
Input pin and signal Output pin and signal
2, IDE_A1 from mux pin 4 18, IDE_A1 / DA0
4, IDE_A2 from mux pin 7 16, IDE_A2 / DA1
6, IDE_A3 from mux pin 9 14, IDE_A3 / DA2

13, IDE_DIOR_n 7, ATA DIOR_n
15, IDE_DIOW_n 5, ATA DIOW_n
17, IDE_RESET_n 3, ATA RESET_n

Ground pins 1 and 19, connect pin 10 to ground, and connect pin 20 to +5 V. Place each source-series resistor after the listed output. Tap IDE_A1..IDE_A3 for the PAL before those resistors.

DMA Cycle Timing

During ACK0_n the single-address R/W describes memory, not the device. DMA_DEV_READ = DMA_CYCLE & !IDE_RW turns a memory write into an ATA read, and DMA_DEV_WRITE = DMA_CYCLE & IDE_RW turns a memory read into an ATA write. IDE_BUF_DIR reverses the transceivers on the same rule, so the PIO interpretation is inverted for both the strobes and the data path.

DMA_CYCLE depends on ACK0_n alone and not on UDS_n or LDS_n. A device-to-memory transfer therefore starts DIOR_n from the acknowledge, before the MC68450 issues data strobes. Deriving the strobe from UDS_n would deadlock: the controller withholds the data strobes until READY, and READY would wait for the strobes.

Single-address DMA intervals at the connector
Interval Adapter value ATA mode 0 requirement
ACK0_n low to DA2..DA0 and CS0_n valid ACT157 select-to-output 14.5 ns plus HCT244 28 ns, 42.5 ns maximum at 4.5 V into 50 pF Address valid before the strobe
Address and chip select before the strobe 199.98 ns minus the 42.5 ns above, 157 ns worst case 70 ns, t1
Strobe asserted before READY reaches the MC68450 Three 5 MHz periods, 599.94 ns minimum 290 ns pulse width, t2
Device read data valid before DRAM samples it 599.94 ns after DIOR_n falls 240 ns derived; see below
DRAM data before the DIOW_n trailing edge The whole strobe, at least 599.94 ns 60 ns setup, t3
DRAM data after the DIOW_n trailing edge DTC_n ends the strobe while the controller still drives AS_n and the data strobes 30 ns hold, t4
Address hold after the strobe The mux holds 000 until ACK0_n rises, after both strobes have ended 20 ns, t9
Cycle time 799.92 ns to READY plus MC68450 synchronization and the memory cycle 600 ns, t0

The 240 ns figure is derived rather than quoted. A device that meets mode 0 cannot know that this host stretches the strobe, so it must present read data early enough for a host that negates DIOR_n at the 290 ns minimum while still meeting the 50 ns read data setup. That leaves 240 ns from the falling edge. READY reaches the MC68450 no earlier than 599.94 ns after the same edge, and the controller then adds its own synchronization before it asserts the data strobes that start the DRAM write. Measure the device strobe-to-data-valid delay during board verification instead of relying on the derivation alone.

IDE_DTACK_n carries no DMA term. The addressed DRAM supplies completion for every single-address cycle, and the adapter contributes READY only. When ACK0_n is inactive the fourth mux channel passes motherboard DTACK_n, which supplies the READY that the MC68450 requires during descriptor fetches. The two sources never drive the pin together, so the PIO completion term is not reused as a DMA completion. The manual's warning on p. 4-16 constrains DTACK rather than READY: a DTACK that arrived before READY would end a device-to-memory cycle with the data strobes never asserted. The DRAM request detector starts on those data strobes, so its DTACK cannot precede them.

A memory-to-device transfer ends DIOW_n on DTC_n, the controller's successful-cycle output. A cycle that takes a bus error suppresses DTC_n, so the write strobe then ends on ACK0_n instead. That ordering does not retract a strobe the device already accepted; section 8 gives the command recovery.

The PIO decode requires IO11_n, and revision 2.2 of Bus and Address Decode gives both I/O decoders an ownership enable. IO11_n therefore cannot assert during a DMA cycle at all, whatever address the controller drives, so a misprogrammed channel cannot start a register access here. The BIOS range check is still the first line; the decoder enable is what makes a firmware mistake harmless.

The CPU-side load added by IDE is one ACT157 input on each of A1..A3, one PAL input on A4, one PAL input on each data strobe, and one HCT04 input on R/W. Each data bit sees one HCT245 port. ACK0_n drives one PAL input, one ACT157 select, and one HCT32 input; DTC_n drives one HCT32 input. Include socket, route, and probe capacitance in the motherboard load audit.

On U_IDE_IRQ, gate 1 inverts processor R/W and gate 2 inverts it again to make IDE_RW. Gate 3 inverts ATA INTRQ to make IDE_IRQ_n. Gates 4 and 5 produce IDE_DMA_END and IDE_READY_n. Ground the remaining input and leave its output open.

6. ATA Connector

J_IDE is a keyed, shrouded, 2-by-20, 2.54 mm header at the board edge. Remove pin 20 for the cable key and mark pin 1. The motherboard supplies signal ground through the cable. The drive power harness supplies +5 V and +12 V through the drive power connector.

Pin Signal Pin Signal

3 DD7 4 DD8
5 DD6 6 DD9
7 DD5 8 DD10
9 DD4 10 DD11
11 DD3 12 DD12
13 DD2 14 DD13
15 DD1 16 DD14
17 DD0 18 DD15
19 Ground 20 Key, pin absent

23 DIOW_n 24 Ground
25 DIOR_n 26 Ground
27 IORDY 28 CSEL, ground at host
29 DMACK_n, 4.7 kohm pull-up 30 Ground

33 DA1 34 PDIAG_n/CBLID_n, no host load

The host does not implement DMA. The pull-up holds DMACK_n inactive. Do not connect DMARQ or IOCS16_n to the processor bus. Device 0 and device 1 use PDIAG_n and DASP_n between themselves during startup, so the host adds no load to those pins.

7. Interrupt and Reset

ATA INTRQ drives one SN74HCT04N inverter. The inverter output, IDE_IRQ_n, drives U_IPL_ENC /I2. A 10 kohm pull-down holds the cable-side input inactive if no drive is connected. Processor level 2 uses autovector $1A. The interrupt handler reads the command block Status register to clear the device request. It reads Alternate Status when it must inspect status without clearing an interrupt.

U_IDE_RESET uses one half of a CD74HCT123E. Tie /A low and /CLR high, and drive B with PERIPH_RESET_n. The rising reset-release edge starts a nominal 4.5 ms pulse with a 100 kohm resistor and 100 nF capacitor. The complementary output is IDE_RESET_PULSE_n. Gate 1 of U_IDE_GATE combines the incoming reset and the pulse before U_IDE_BUS drives the cable. Both signals also inhibit the PAL cycle terms, so neither a PIO access nor an ACK0_n cycle can drive ATA strobes while the drive is held in reset. 

IDE_RESET_n = PERIPH_RESET_n AND IDE_RESET_PULSE_n

The direct term asserts reset without waiting for the monostable. The pulse term holds reset after release, so the 12.4 microsecond CPU RESET instruction produces a pulse longer than the ATA 25 microsecond minimum. The board's 100 ms power-on reset also reaches the drive. Firmware waits for both devices to finish diagnostics and leave BSY before issuing a command. Ground /CLR on the unused monostable half and fix both trigger inputs.

8. Firmware Rules

  1. Wait for BSY to clear after reset. Apply the ATA device-selection delays.
  2. Probe device 0 and device 1. Issue IDENTIFY DEVICE. If the device aborts it and reports an ATAPI signature, issue IDENTIFY PACKET DEVICE.
  3. Read capability words before choosing CHS, LBA28, LBA48, sector size, removable-media handling, or packet commands.
  4. Keep every command in ATA PIO mode 0 with the DIOR and DIOW protocol. Do not enable multiword DMA or UDMA. Motherboard DMA carries the same PIO data cycles, and ATA DMARQ and DMACK stay unused.
  5. Transfer the data register with 16-bit word accesses. The crossed lanes put ATA sector byte zero at the lower memory address, so neither PIO nor DMA swaps sector words.
  6. Byte-swap IDENTIFY numeric words when interpreting them. Treat ATA string fields, ATAPI command packets, and ATAPI response data under each format's own rules rather than one blanket swap.
  7. Use byte accesses at even addresses with UDS_n for task-file and control registers. Poll BSY, DRQ, DF, and ERR at each command phase and impose a software timeout measured in milliseconds or seconds.
  8. Install an autovector level-2 handler before enabling ATA interrupts. Polling remains valid while nIEN is set in Device Control.
  9. Start MC68450 channel 0 only after the command has reached its data phase: BSY clear, DRQ set, ERR and DF clear, and the direction matching the command. Program the channel as a 16-bit implicitly addressed device with acknowledge and ready, internal maximum-rate requests, and word operands.
  10. Bound each activation to the permitted data phase and to at most 32 words. A single-sector command allows 256 words; an ATAPI packet transfer allows the byte count the device reports. Re-read Status and DRQ between activations. Do not let the channel auto-request across a sector or packet boundary.
  11. Treat an ATA command as indeterminate after a DMA bus error. A suppressed DTC_n does not undo a strobe the device already accepted. Read Status, drain or reset the interrupted command, release the pinned buffer, then re-issue.
  12. Include command issue, status polling, interrupt service, and chunk restarts in any throughput figure. The channel moves data only inside the data phase.

ATAPI support needs the PACKET command and the packet command set in firmware. The motherboard supplies the same register, interrupt, data, and DMA paths to ATA and ATAPI devices.

Fit one 100 nF ceramic capacitor at each IC supply pair and one 10 uF bulk capacitor near J_IDE. The IC families and packages predate the project's 1994 cutoff. The PAL uses a socketed PLCC; the remaining ICs use plastic DIP packages.

10. Layout

  • Put J_IDE at the board edge and keep the keyed cable clear of the expansion cards.
  • Put both HCT245 parts and the 33 ohm data resistors between the processor bus and the connector.
  • Put U_IDE_BUS and its series resistors beside the connector.
  • Keep each data route short and match the paths within the 16-bit group. Route a ground return beside the cable interface.
  • Keep IDE_IORDY and INTRQ away from clock traces. Place their pull resistors at the motherboard receivers.
  • Put U_IDE_DA_MUX between the PAL and U_IDE_BUS so the selected address reaches the cable driver without a detour.
  • Group U_IDE_GATE, U_IDE_OR, and U_IDE_IRQ beside the PAL. Keep ACK0_n, DTC_n, BGACK_n, DTACK_n, and PCL0_n short between this cluster and the MC68450, and away from the cable edge.

11. Verification

Required checks
Check Pass condition
PAL build Unrun. No compatible CUPL fitter is installed. On a machine that has one, the listing must fit the fixed pins in a PALCE20V8-compatible fuse map within eight product terms per output, and programmer verification must pass.
Idle bus Both chip selects, both strobes, and IDE_DTACK_n stay high with no slot-11 cycle.
PIO timing Measured address setup, strobe width, recovery, and cycle time meet PIO mode 0 at both cable connectors.
IORDY Holding IORDY low keeps the CPU waiting and keeps the active ATA strobe low until IORDY rises or the motherboard timeout expires.
Byte lanes Task-file byte accesses use even addresses and D15..D8. A data-register word test preserves all 16 bit positions across the crossing, and a sector read stores ATA byte zero at the lower memory address with no software swap.
Device combinations Device 0 alone, device 1 alone, and two devices enumerate with jumper and Cable Select configurations.
Media types One ATA disk, one ATAPI optical drive, a 44-pin disk through an adapter, and CompactFlash through a True IDE adapter complete repeated reads.
Interrupt INTRQ produces level 2, acknowledge produces autovector $1A, and a Status read clears the request.
Reset Power-on, push-button, watchdog, and CPU RESET assertion reach connector pin 1 with the required pulse width.
DMA address selection ACK0_n forces DA2..DA0 to 000 and CS0_n active with CS1_n high, and the measured setup ahead of the strobe exceeds 70 ns at the connector.
DMA direction A memory write drives DIOR_n and turns the transceivers toward the processor; a memory read drives DIOW_n and turns them toward the cable. Neither strobe appears without ACK0_n or a slot-11 cycle.
READY path PCL0_n follows the QE and IORDY term during ACK0_n, follows motherboard DTACK_n during descriptor fetches, and stays high while the processor owns the bus. Holding IORDY low delays READY and the DRAM write until IORDY rises or the motherboard timeout expires.
Device data validity Measured device strobe-to-data-valid delay is shorter than the interval from DIOR_n falling to the DRAM write, for every drive on the acceptance list.
Write strobe end DTC_n ends DIOW_n while DRAM data is still driven, and the measured hold exceeds 30 ns.
DMA faults An injected bus error during a channel-0 cycle suppresses DTC_n, aborts the channel, and leaves the command recoverable by the documented sequence. A channel deliberately programmed with a slot-11 address asserts no IO11_n and drives no ATA strobe.
Mixed traffic Repeated 32-word activations interleave with floppy and expansion channels, DRAM refresh, and CPU PIO without data corruption or a missed status phase.

  • INCITS T13, AT Attachment with Packet Interface - 7, Volume 2, parallel transport signals, connector, register selection, reset, and PIO timing.
  • Microchip, AVR32115: AVR32 AP7 Linux ATA driver, 16-bit memory-mapped PATA adapter and two-device PIO operation.
  • Advanced Micro Devices, PALCE20V8 Family, PLCC pinout, combinational mode, timing, and electrical limits.
  • Texas Instruments, CD74HC164/CD74HCT164, asynchronous clear and shift timing; SN74HCT245 and SN74HCT244, bus buffering.
  • Texas Instruments, CD74ACT157, common select, active-low strobe, TTL-compatible input levels, and select-to-output switching limits; SN74HCT08 and SN74HCT32, added gate delays and drive.
  • Motorola, MC68450 Direct Memory Access Controller, single-address transfers, the acknowledge-and-ready device protocol, the descriptor-fetch READY requirement in Figure 4-12 on pp. 4-17 and 4-18, and DTC_n behaviour on a failed cycle. The board-level connections are in DMA Controller.
  • Motorola, M68000 User's Manual, asynchronous bus cycles, byte strobes, reset, interrupts, and autovectors.
